subject: Ordering & stacking variables in bar plots

messages.author: faa147d63a6c0a2d
messages.subject: Ordering & stacking variables in bar plots
parts:
Hello group,

I'm having trouble with something I thought would be very simple &
would appreciate some advice!

I want to make some barplots of some ready-summarised data concerning
admission rates to different hospitals. In this simplified example
there are four hospitals and admissions of two types: inpatient (IP) &
day cases (DC).

#Construct example data frame (in wide format to start with)
Hosp = c("Cambridge","Leeds","Birmingham","Southampton")
IP = c(240, 210, 160, 520)
DC = c(1240, 990, 1150, 460)
adm.df = data.frame(Hosp, IP, DC)

#Make basic plot of IP admissions
qplot(Hosp, IP, data = adm.df, geom = "bar")

The first thing I want to do is to order the plot by a variable, e.g.
IP admission rates - this is easy

#Make basic plot of IP admissions ordered by IP admissions
qplot(reorder(Hosp, IP), IP, data = adm.df, geom = "bar")

The next thing I want to do is to stack IP & DC rates in the bar plot
- with the data in wide format this seems tricky - I can plot the sum

#Make plot of the sum of IP + DC
qplot(Hosp, IP + DC, data = adm.df, geom = "bar")

But I don't know if there is any way to make the variables stack
directly from this kind of data frame

Reshaping the data into long format makes it easier

#Reshape data
library(reshape)
madm.df <- melt(adm.df)
names(madm.df) <- c("Hospital","IP_DC","Admissions")

#Now stacking is no trouble
qplot(Hospital, Admissions, data = madm.df, geom = "bar", fill =
IP_DC)

#And ordering the plot by *total* admissions is easy
qplot(reorder(Hospital, Admissions), Admissions, data = madm.df, geom
= "bar", fill = IP_DC)

But how about if I want to go back to ordering the factor Hospital by
just one element of Admissions? e.g. order by just IP admission rates.
This seems hard...

So my two bar plotting questions are:
1) Can I stack two variables from a wide format data frame without
reshaping the data frame first?
2) How can I order a stacked bar plot by just one element in the
stack?

Hope this makes sense

Thanks for any advice!

Andrew Graham
Dept. of Neurology
Addenbrooke's Hospital

messages.author: 9e1d805a26f6d719
messages.subject: Re: Ordering & stacking variables in bar plots
parts: Very clear question! Slightly complex answer...

> So my two bar plotting questions are:
> 1) Can I stack two variables from a wide format data frame without
> reshaping the data frame first?
Nope. ggplot2 likes long-format data frames.

> 2) How can I order a stacked bar plot by just one element in the
> stack?

One way to do it would be to make Hospital an ordered factor, with the
order based on the other variable. Like this (but ideally with better
variable names!):

> x <- subset(madm.df, subset=IP_DC=="IP")
> x[order(x$Admissions), ]
Hospital IP_DC Admissions
3 Birmingham IP 160
2 Leeds IP 210
1 Cambridge IP 240
4 Southampton IP 520
> y <- x[order(x$Admissions), ]$Hospital
> y
[1] Birmingham Leeds Cambridge Southampton
Levels: Birmingham Cambridge Leeds Southampton
> madm.df$Hospital <- factor(madm.df$Hospital, levels=y, ordered=TRUE)
> madm.df
Hospital IP_DC Admissions
1 Cambridge IP 240
2 Leeds IP 210
3 Birmingham IP 160
4 Southampton IP 520
5 Cambridge DC 1240
6 Leeds DC 990
7 Birmingham DC 1150
8 Southampton DC 460
> madm.df$Hospital
[1] Cambridge Leeds Birmingham Southampton Cambridge
Leeds
[7] Birmingham Southampton
Levels: Birmingham < Leeds < Cambridge < Southampton
> ggplot(madm.df, aes(Hospital, Admissions, fill=IP_DC)) + geom_bar(stat="identity")

ggplot is smart enough to know that if your variable is an ordered
factor, you want it plotted in that order.

There may be other ways of doing it, of course...

(I also will add that it's usually easier to understand what's going
on, and to fix problems in your plot, if you use the ggplot syntax
rather than the qplot syntax. Hadley may disagree. :) )

-Harlan

messages.subject: Re: Ordering & stacking variables in bar plots
parts:
Excellent! Harlan, thank you very much - that's just what I wanted.

It does seem a shame, however, that one has to jump through so many
hoops to solve this. The data frame consists of one factor of four
levels and then eight numbers in two groups of four each - all the
information required to make this plot is explicitly given right there
in the structure of the data frame and the eight values within it.
Presumably (if I had the competence) I could turn your code into a
function to do this ordering for me and then embed it within the call
to ggplot / qplot?

I guess I should develop my R skills and do just that.

Cheers

Andrew

messages.author: 9e1d805a26f6d719
messages.subject: Re: Ordering & stacking variables in bar plots
parts:
Great, glad I could help.

I tend to think that ggplot is doing more-or-less the right thing.
Ordering is something that can be done within a data frame, so it's
better to assume that whoever created the data frame knew how they
wanted to order things. So yeah, writing a function to reorder the
factors based on other values sounds like a good plan going forward,
if you're going to be doing this same operation repeatedly!

-Harlan
